rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 0 is still the best design (score 53.02). Its 60 trials all ended off track, and the s-bend progress was 0.1475 in every iteration tested, across kp 2.5 to 4.5, kd 0.15 to 1.0, base speed 1.3 to 1.6 and both sensor sizes. The critique is right that the draft's claim that kp was raised in every lower-scoring run is wrong. Iteration 2 kept kp 3.5 and changed only sensor size, so the kp 'overcorrection' argument has no direct support. I therefore do not present kp 2.5 as a likely improvement. I keep it only as a clean one-factor probe, because the s-bend failure point has not moved under any gain change, and a clean test is the only way to learn whether kp sets it.

What I kept, changed and rejected after the round-2 critique:
(1) Kept the single change kp 3.5 to 2.5. All other values equal iteration 0: kd 0.15, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5, line_loss last_direction, weights [1, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1], sensors at y=0.06 with x at +0.04, +0.02, 0, -0.02, -0.04, sensor_size 0.012, and unchanged geometry. This is attributable to kp alone.
(2) Retracted the 'kp raised in every lower run' premise. I changed the rationale, not the design, to say so.
(3) Accepted the critique's point that a lower kp could increase steady lateral error, so the result can go either way. I now state the direction in advance. On the oval, rms_error and max_error should not fall; if they rise with progress flat, kp was supplying needed correction and I revert.
(4) Rejected the speed cut for now. Completion needs about 1.5 m/s average, and nothing has shown speed is the limit. This is a judgement, and I say so. Speed will be tested alone after the kp result if the failure point stays fixed.
(5) Accepted that the decision rule must name the track and metric. The oval alone moved in iteration 2, so a score change driven by the oval does not count as a general gain.

Decision rule for the next revision. Use the three-track mean score and the s-bend progress. (a) If the s-bend progress rises above 0.1475, or the three-track mean score rises above 53.0 with no oval-only driver, keep kp 2.5 and test kd alone (0.15 to 0.4). (b) If the s-bend progress is 0.1475 and the score falls below 53.0, revert kp to 3.5 and test kd alone. (c) If the s-bend progress stays at 0.1475 with the score unchanged, kp does not set the failure point. The next test is line_loss, changing last_direction to search_right for one race.

Expected result: score within about 0.5 of 53.0 and s-bend progress at 0.1475. A large gain is not expected from one gain change; the purpose is to locate the lever.
